thoughts.label: Fifteen minutes daily
thoughts.text: Short daily practice beats one long weekend session for building finger memory.
thoughts.prompt: How long should a practice session be?

thoughts.label: Slow is smooth
thoughts.text: Practise new changes at half speed until they are clean, then speed up.

thoughts.label: Metronome every time
thoughts.text: Always practise with a metronome so timing grows with technique.
thoughts.prompt: What should every practice session use?

thoughts.label: Record and listen
thoughts.text: Recording a take each week shows progress the ear misses while playing.
thoughts.prompt: How do you notice slow progress?

thoughts.label: Warm up fingers
thoughts.text: Two minutes of spider exercises prevents strain before chord work.

thoughts.label: When to stop?
thoughts.text: Is it better to stop when tired or push through sore fingertips?
thoughts.prompt: What is still undecided about sore fingers?

thoughts.label: Open chords first
thoughts.text: Learn G, C, D, E minor and A minor before any barre chord.
thoughts.prompt: Which chords come before barre chords?

thoughts.label: Anchor finger
thoughts.text: Keep one finger on the string while changing chords to move faster.

thoughts.label: Thumb behind neck
thoughts.text: Thumb behind the neck, not over it, makes barre chords possible.
thoughts.prompt: Where does the thumb go for barre chords?

thoughts.label: Barre F later
thoughts.text: Tackle the F barre chord after a month of open chords.
thoughts.prompt: When should the F barre chord start?

thoughts.label: Mute with palm
thoughts.text: Light palm muting cleans up strumming between chord changes.
thoughts.prompt: How do you clean up strumming?

thoughts.label: Power chords useful?
thoughts.text: Should power chords come before full barre chords for rock songs?
thoughts.prompt: Which chord type is still an open choice?

thoughts.label: Learn the fretboard
thoughts.text: Knowing note names on the low E string unlocks every barre shape.

thoughts.label: Major scale pattern
thoughts.text: Whole, whole, half, whole, whole, whole, half builds every major scale.
thoughts.prompt: What step pattern builds a major scale?

thoughts.label: Keys share chords
thoughts.text: Songs in one key reuse the same few chords, so learn by key.
thoughts.prompt: Why learn songs grouped by key?

thoughts.label: Circle of fifths
thoughts.text: Use the circle of fifths to find which chords sound good together.
thoughts.prompt: What tool shows which chords fit together?

thoughts.label: Ear before tabs
thoughts.text: Try to find a melody by ear before reading the tab.
thoughts.prompt: What comes before reading a tab?

thoughts.label: Read notation too?
thoughts.text: Is standard notation worth learning, or are tabs enough for now?
thoughts.prompt: Which reading skill is still undecided?

thoughts.label: Lighter strings
thoughts.text: Light gauge strings are kinder on beginner fingertips.

thoughts.label: Tune every session
thoughts.text: An electronic tuner at the start of each session keeps ears honest.

thoughts.label: Action matters
thoughts.text: A shop setup lowering the action made chords far easier.

thoughts.label: Capo for keys
thoughts.text: A capo lets you play songs in new keys with the same shapes.

thoughts.label: Upgrade later?
thoughts.text: When is the right time to buy a better guitar?

threads.why: Slow changes need an anchor finger
Open chords live in common keys
Sore fingers partly a string choice
